_schema.applies_to: matcher on {program, metrics, subgroups}; null = any
_schema.basis: traceability: source Guidance/Notes sheets, the HBAI methodology report, a GitHub issue, or a measured diagnostic in this repo's data

annotations.text: HBAI is categorically held out — the UK analogue of the census-spm permanent-holdout doctrine: survey-derived poverty statistics are never calibration targets, so every cell scores calibration_relationship=held_out. PolicyEngine UK's enhanced FRS is built from the same underlying survey, and its calibration targets include income and demographic aggregates that co-move with poverty rates; that adjacency is a construction fact to record on comparisons (expect co-movement-driven deviations), never grounds to reclassify a cell as consumed_as_target.
annotations.basis: scorecard issue #35; census-spm lane doctrine (2026-08-02); policyengine-uk calibration target registry

annotations.text: HBAI is measured survey income, not simulated entitlement: reported receipt (informed by admin data from 2021/22), reported housing costs, and survey equivalence scales. PE poverty rates are simulated tax/benefit outcomes on reweighted FRS microdata with calibrated take-up. Divergence decomposes into data (survey vs enhanced-FRS), income concept, and simulated-vs-reported receipt channels.

There is a break in series from 2021/22: integrated survey and benefit admin data, and a change in the absolute-poverty base year. Pre- and post-break years are not directly comparable, and DWP flags the FYE 2021 (COVID) survey year separately. Score each year against this release's restated series.
annotations.basis: Series-break note on every parsed sheet; Notes sheet

annotations.text: Summary rows are GB before 2002/03 and UK from 2002/03 (the FRS did not cover Northern Ireland earlier); the geography field tracks the switch, and early NI cells in regional tables are suppressed. A PE counterpart must match the geography field per row, not assume UK throughout.
annotations.basis: FRS (GB)/FRS (UK) row markers in the summary tables

annotations.text: All region/country rows are 3-year rolling averages (periods like '2022/23-2024/25'); single-year regional estimates are not published due to sample size. A comparable PE counterpart averages three simulation years with matching uprating, not one year.

Rates are published to whole percentage points (fractions here carry ±0.005 rounding) and counts to 0.1 million (±50,000). '[low]' cells (< 0.05 million) and '[u]' small-sample cells are suppressed. DWP marks most recent-year movements not statistically significant; deltas inside sampling error should not be scored as divergence.
annotations.basis: Guidance sheet; uncertainty tables in the same publication

annotations.text: Low income is 60% of median equivalised net disposable household income (OECD-companion scales; AHC deducts housing costs and uses the AHC equivalence variant). PE poverty output must use HBAI's household sharing unit, equivalence scales, and BHC/AHC definitions — not benefit-unit income or unequivalised measures. Absolute low income is anchored to the FYE 2011 median in real terms (rebased at the series break), not a fixed basket.
annotations.basis: HBAI methodology report FYE 2025, income-measure definitions

annotations.text: The vendored two_child campaign family scores child-poverty-count changes against Resolution Foundation claims derived from an HBAI-consistent poverty line; those PE runs used a fixed baseline relative-AHC line and an HBAI-dependent-child proxy. When those rows attach (#33), this source's children AHC series is the level benchmark the deltas ride on.
